# QuantaAlpha: An Evolutionary Framework for LLM-Driven Alpha Mining

arXiv [2602.07085](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07085) · v1 2026-02-06 · latest 2026-05-18

> **Machine-extracted method card.** The gloss column was written by `claude-opus-5-5` (effort medium) on 2026-10-23 from the html text of the paper. Every quote was checked by a program to be a passage of that text; the gloss has not been checked by a person. "Not found" means the model did not find the item in the text it was given, not that the paper omits it.

| Field | Gloss | Quote from the paper |
|---|---|---|
| **task** | Automated LLM-driven alpha factor mining that improves factors via trajectory-level evolution (mutation and crossover) under noisy, non-stationary markets. | “we propose QuantaAlpha, an evolutionary alpha mining framework that treats each end-to-end mining run as a trajectory and improves factors via trajectory-level mutation and crossover.” |
| **architecture** | Multi-agent pipeline: diversified planning initialization, idea agent for hypotheses, factor agent producing symbolic AST expressions compiled to code with consistency verifier and complexity/redundancy gates, evaluation agent, self-evolution via mutation/crossover, final factor pool fed to LightGBM. | “Overview of the QuantaAlpha framework, which consists of four core components: (A) Diversified Planning Initialization for candidate hypotheses, (B) Factor Realization that instantiates hypotheses into executable factors with constraint gating, (C) Self-Evolution with mutation and crossover over evaluated trajectories” |
| **data** | Daily OHLCV+vwap data via Qlib for CSI 300 (300 large-cap A-shares); zero-shot transfer to CSI 500 and S&P 500; target is next-day return. | “Factor construction utilizes six basic features—open, high, low, close, volume, and vwap—to predict the next-day return” |
| **window** | Train Jan 1 2016–Dec 31 2020, validation Jan 1–Dec 31 2021, test Jan 1 2022–Dec 26 2025 (same for all markets). | “We adopt a chronological split with training (Jan. 1, 2016 to Dec. 31, 2020), validation (Jan. 1, 2021 to Dec. 31, 2021), and testing (Jan. 1, 2022 to Dec. 26, 2025).” |
| **models** | Backbone LLMs Qwen3-235B, DeepSeek-V3.2, Gemini-3-Pro-Preview, Claude-4.5-Sonnet, GPT-5.2 (DeepSeek-V3.2 default); LightGBM as downstream model. | “we evaluate multiple backbone LLMs, including Qwen3-235B, DeepSeek-V3.2, Gemini-3-Pro-Preview, Claude-4.5-Sonnet, and GPT-5.2. Unless otherwise specified, all other LLM-based experiments in this paper adopt DeepSeek-V3.2 for consistency and fair comparison.” |
| **baselines** | ML models (Linear, MLP, LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, DoubleEnsemble), deep learning (GRU, LSTM, Transformer, TRA), factor libraries (Alpha158, Alpha360), LLM agents RD-Agent and AlphaAgent. | “We compare QuantaAlpha against four baseline categories: traditional machine learning models, deep learning time-series models, classical factor libraries, and LLM-based factor research agents, including RD-Agent and AlphaAgent.” |
| **headline_result** | With GPT-5.2 on CSI 300 test period (2022–2025): IC 0.0472, ARR 4.68%, MDD 11.80%; transfer cumulative excess return about 40.28% (CSI 500) and 19.1% (S&P 500) over four years. | “Using GPT-5.2, QuantaAlpha achieves the best IC at 0.0472, delivers an ARR of 4.68%, and maintains a low MDD of 11.80%.” |
| **costs** | Buy 0.05%, sell 0.15% (0.20% round-trip), sensitivity at 1.5x and 2.0x; ~1.8M tokens and ~20 hours per main run via hosted APIs. | “we adopt a standard transaction-cost setting with a buying cost of 0.05% (open_cost=0.0005) and a selling cost of 0.15% (close_cost=0.0015), corresponding to a 0.20% round-trip cost.” |
| **uncertainty** | Three initial seed combinations (IC std 0.0021); daily IC t-tests over 966 trading days with 95% CIs, p<0.001. | “In particular, the standard deviations of IC and Rank IC are 0.0021 and 0.0024, respectively, suggesting that QuantaAlpha’s performance is not driven by a fortuitously selected seed set.” |
| **leakage_controls** | Factor pool admission uses only 2021 validation RankIC; 2022–2025 test window never accessed during evolution or pool construction; chronological split. | “The RankIC gate for pool admission is computed exclusively on the 2021 validation period; the 2022–2025 test window is never accessed during evolution or pool construction.” |
| **limitations** | Real-world deployment would need additional transaction-cost modeling, risk control and live trading validation; performance decays after ~15 iterations. | “although real-world deployment would require additional transaction-cost modeling, risk control, and live trading validation.” |
| **release** | Data and code released on GitHub. | “Data and code are available at https://github.com/QuantaAlpha/QuantaAlpha.” |
